newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia poll body said seeks Megawati settlement.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia poll body said seeks Megawati settlement.

text.p: Indonesia's election commission is pushing for an out-of-court settlement with ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri who is challenging a ban on taking part in next year's polls, her lawyer said on Wednesday.

Megawati's law suit against the General Election Institute (LPU) and its chairman, Interior Minister Yogie Memet, was adjourned on Wednesday to allow out-of-court talks, her chief lawyer, R.O. Tambunan, told Reuters after the 15-minute hearing.
"We have already read our suit but the lawyers from the LPU have asked for a two-week adjournment to look for a negotiated solution," Tambunan said.
"It's usual for civil cases, but it is they who are looking for an out-of-court settlement solution."

A government-backed rebel faction ousted Megawati as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in June, and the LPU refused to accept her list of candidates for the elections due next May.
Tambunan said Megawati's case was based upon the premise that she remained the legal leader of the PDI.

Another lawsuit in which Megawati is challenging her ouster is before the Jakarta High Court pending an appeal after a lower court said it did not have the authority to rule on an internal party matter.
In September, LPU officials received a list of candidates from the government-approved PDI leader Surjadi and rejected a similar list from Megawati's supporters.
"Megawati has put forward election candidates and we are asking the judges to force the LPU and the Interior Minister to receive these candidates," Tambunan said.
Political analysts have said the government wanted Megawati removed from control of the PDI over concern she might draw votes from the ruling Golkar party in the elections.
Golkar won 68 percent of the vote in the last elections in 1992. The Moslem-oriented United Development Party took 17 percent of the vote, and the Christian-national PDI 15 percent.
